facts.subject: main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_Fall_FromParamY

facts.subject: main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ParticleRender
facts.value: When particle and particle->appsrt are non-null, the callback copies translation, scale, and rotation from the current AppSRT into locals, detaches that AppSRT through psRemoveParticleAppSRT, and attaches a newly allocated status-1 AppSRT through psAddParticleAppSRT_begin. facts.subject: main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Update
facts.value: Reads the effect's HSD_JObj from gobj->hsd_obj and its EF_Effect record from GObj user data. state_flags controls early processing; lifetime is decremented and may send the GObj to removal. When scale inheritance is enabled and attach_jobj exists, a non-root attachment supplies scale from its world matrix after any dirty matrix is rebuilt, while a root attachment supplies its local scale; the attachment's Y component is then copied to X and Z and written as a uniform effect scale. Finally the effect JObj hierarchy is animated and EF_Effect.update receives the effect record when non-null.
facts.reason: PauseAll writes (state_flags & 0x80) | 1 for owner matches in both lists. Update switches on the full byte: exactly 1 increments to 2 and still runs this tick; exactly 2 returns. States 0x81 and 0x82 do not enter either case. ResumeAll preserves only 0x80. Thus the preserved asynchronous-state bit prevents these pause cases from matching; no masking is performed by Update. Nonzero u16 lifetime predecrements and removal returns before later work. Scale inheritance uses non-root attachment matrix scale or root local scale, broadcasts Y uniformly, then animates root/non-instance descendants and calls update.

entities.role: `efLib_SetParamAlpha` and `efLib_SetParamGfxId` associate an owner GObj with alpha and graphics-ID values in one of eight `EF_ParamEntry` slots. This function selects that slot by comparing its GObj with `effect->parent_gobj`, obtains material texture objects through the effect GObj's child JObj/DObj/MObj hierarchy, and copies the stored alpha into `tobj->tev->konst.a`. Graphics ID 0x417 redirects the initial write to the next texture object, while ID 0x419 additionally copies the alpha into the materials of six successive sibling JObjs. The callback scans at most eight parameter slots and stops after the first slot owned by `effect->parent_gobj`; if no slot matches, it leaves the effect unchanged. A normal matching entry updates one TEV alpha channel, graphics ID 0x417 first advances to the second texture object, and graphics ID 0x419 updates the initial channel plus one channel on each of six following sibling JObjs. entities.role: Consumes the effect's GObj to obtain its JObj, reads that JObj's current translation and X/Y rotations, and treats effect->params.y as mutable vertical velocity. It subtracts 0.2 from that velocity, adds sin(rotation_y) and cos(rotation_y) to the X and Z positions respectively, adds the updated velocity to Y, and adds 0.5 to X rotation; the resulting transform is consumed by the effect rendering and animation pipeline. On every active invocation, the callback first lowers the stored vertical velocity by 0.2 and then applies the new value to vertical position, so repeated updates produce constant downward acceleration. Simultaneously it advances one unit per update in the horizontal direction selected by Y rotation and accumulates 0.5 of X rotation per update. It contains no termination guard; lifetime expiration and pause suppression are handled by efLib_Update before callback dispatch.

entities.role: When particle and particle->appsrt are non-null, the callback copies translation, scale, and rotation from the current AppSRT into locals, detaches that AppSRT through psRemoveParticleAppSRT, and attaches a newly allocated status-1 AppSRT through psAddParticleAppSRT_begin. On success it copies the saved transform into the new record. On allocation failure it instead writes cmdWait = 0, size = 0.0, and life = 1 to the particle. A null particle or a particle without an AppSRT is left unchanged. Otherwise the particle transitions from its old AppSRT attachment to a fresh attachment carrying identical transform values. If allocation fails after the old attachment has been removed, the particle enters a terminal visual state with no wait, zero size, and one remaining life unit. Copies SRT values but no other state or matrix; it performs no drawing. The local callback/vector return void, while HSD_PSUserFunc hooks return int. The void-pointer setter does not establish signature or ABI compatibility.

entities.role: Receives the EF_Effect from efLib_Update, follows effect->gobj to the effect root JObj and then its child pointer, reads the child's current translation.z, adds 2.0, and writes the accumulated value back through the JObj translation setter. entities.role: On each active effect update, the callback reads the JObj's current X/Y/Z translation and the effect's parameter vector, subtracts 0.1 from params.y in place, then writes X + params.x, Y + the updated params.y, and Z + params.z back to the JObj. The mutated Y parameter is retained in EF_Effect and therefore becomes the vertical increment consumed by the next invocation. Repeated invocations integrate a discrete gravity-like trajectory: X and Z advance by their stored offsets, while the Y increment decreases by 0.1 before every position update. Thus vertical motion progressively bends downward, with params.y crossing through zero and becoming increasingly negative unless another routine changes it.

entities.role: The callback reads `effect->user_data`, `effect->gobj`, `expire_flags`, and `lifetime`. A non-null user-data JObj contributes the sign of `scale.x`, which becomes a root-model Y rotation of -π/2 for negative scale and +π/2 otherwise. The expiration branch writes lifetime 11, clears `effect->update`, and requests animation frame 65 across the effect's JObj hierarchy; otherwise, lifetime 1 is rewritten to 6 and frame 60 is requested across that hierarchy. The callback has two transition modes. When `expire_flags` is not `EF_DOES_NOT_EXPIRE`, its first invocation makes the transition one-shot by setting lifetime to 11, clearing the update callback, and requesting animation frame 65; subsequent effect updates count that lifetime down to removal without invoking this callback again. When the flag equals `EF_DOES_NOT_EXPIRE`, the callback remains installed, and an invocation that observes lifetime 1 changes it to 6 and requests animation frame 60. A null user-data pointer suppresses only the orientation update, not either transition mode. Expiration tests the stored low byte. Current model animation can reset transforms before this callback.

entities.role: Reads `effect->parent_gobj` to obtain the owning Fighter and `effect->gobj` to obtain the rendered HSD_JObj. It computes `M_PI_2_F - fighter->mv.co.common.x4.x`, tests `fighter->facing_dir`, and writes the effect JObj's Y and Z rotations: negative-facing fighters receive Y = -π/2 and Z = +(π/2 - x4.x), while nonnegative-facing fighters receive Y = +π/2 and Z = -(π/2 - x4.x). Each invocation overwrites the effect JObj's Y and Z orientation rather than incrementing it. The fighter's facing sign selects one of two mirrored states: left-facing uses negative quarter-turn Y and positive computed Z tilt, while right-facing or zero uses positive quarter-turn Y and negative computed Z tilt.

entities.role: Reads the primary effect GObj, the next linked EF_Effect's GObj, and the parent fighter. From the fighter it consumes motion_id, command-variable bit 0 of cmd_vars[2], move variable x10, and the current floor normal. It writes JOBJ_HIDDEN on the second effect hierarchy and writes the same Z rotation to both effect hierarchies, using -atan2f(floor.normal.x, floor.normal.y) when both alignment guards pass and 0 otherwise. During motion 359, the callback clears JOBJ_HIDDEN on the second effect hierarchy; in every other motion it hides that hierarchy. The second model is effect->next->gobj, not a child JObj. common.x10 is UNK_T and cast to s32; do not infer a floating scalar.

entities.signature: EF_Effect* efLib_CreateGenerator_AppSRT_SetPos(int gfx_id, HSD_GObj* gobj, HSD_JObj* jobj, Vec3* vec)
entities.role: The function creates a generic effect with descriptor ID 0 under gobj, stores jobj in effect->attach_jobj and a value copy of *vec in effect->params, and attaches the gfx_id-selected generator to GET_JOBJ(effect->gobj). During later active effect updates, efLib_Cb_AccumOffset_FromParams reads the attachment's current translation, adds the stored x/y/z offset, and writes the sum to the effect JObj; the attached generator consequently receives that moving transform through its AppSRT-enabled attachment. If efLib_Create fails, the function returns NULL without initializing an attachment or generator. Once an effect exists, it is returned even if generator creation or AppSRT allocation fails; the helper destroys an AppSRT-less generator and nulls only its local output. For a successfully configured effect, each active update recomputes its position from the attachment and fixed offset, while the library's paused state suppresses that callback and therefore freezes this positional following until updates resume.

main/melee/ef/eflib:.bss.value: When efLib_Create loads an effect whose descriptor has joint, material, or shape animation data, it stores the effect JObj at efLib_AnimQueue[efLib_AnimCount] through an HSD_JObj** view and increments efLib_AnimCount. Initialization marks all eight parameter slots unused and gives them an alpha default of 255. efLib_SetParamAlpha and efLib_SetParamGfxId first search those slots for the supplied owner GObj, then for a free slot, and update the selected record; efLib_Cb_ApplyStoredAlpha later finds the record whose GObj matches an effect's parent_gobj and applies its alpha to the effect's TEV constant-alpha state, with graphics IDs 0x417 and 0x419 selecting specialized texture or child-model handling.
main/melee/ef/eflib:.bss.rationale: The current creation path remains the animation-queue producer, while initialization, setters, and the alpha callback preserve the complete parameter-table producer and consumer flow.

main/melee/ef/eflib:.bss.value: A 0xC0-byte BSS layout containing a 0x80-byte animation-registration region at 0x80458EE0 and an eight-entry EF_ParamEntry table at 0x80458F60. The first region is declared as EF_ParamEntry[16] for source/code-generation reasons but is logically accessed as HSD_JObj*[32]; the second is EF_ParamEntry[8], where each 8-byte entry contains a pointer, a 16-bit graphics ID, and a 16-bit alpha value.
main/melee/ef/eflib:.bss.rationale: The head header still establishes EF_ParamEntry as an 8-byte pointer, graphics-ID, and alpha record. The head source declares sixteen such entries at 0x80458EE0 followed by eight at 0x80458F60, while effect creation continues to access the first region through HSD_JObj** and enforce a logical capacity of 32 registrations.

main/melee/ef/eflib:.bss.value: A parameter-table slot is free when its GObj field is null. Initialization resets every slot to free with fully opaque alpha. Animation registrations advance a separate global count, and reaching 32 registrations triggers the "Over Anime Call" assertion.
main/melee/ef/eflib:.bss.rationale: The head source preserves the initialization defaults, two-pass slot selection, full-table return, animation-count increment, and capacity assertion.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ParticleRen.rationale: The callback body still performs the complete snapshot, detach, replacement, restore, and failure sequence. The AppSRT implementation confirms attachment allocation and reference-counted removal semantics.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ParticleRen.value: Preserves a particle effect's visible position, orientation, and scale while separating it from its previous, potentially shared particle-system transform attachment; when that separation cannot be completed, the effect is hidden and rapidly retired.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ParticleRen.rationale: AppSRT carries translation, rotation, and scale and is reference-counted. The callback transfers those values to a fresh attachment, while failure sets zero size and one remaining life unit.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ParticleRen.value: Particle callback with signature void (HSD_Particle* particle). The callback table containing it is an array of functions taking HSD_Particle* and returning void.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ParticleRen.rationale: The head source preserves both the exact function signature and the adjacent typed three-entry callback vector.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ParticleRen.value: Replaces an eligible particle's existing AppSRT attachment with a newly allocated AppSRT while preserving its translation, rotation, and scale; if replacement allocation fails, it suppresses and expires the particle.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ParticleRen.rationale: The current callback still snapshots the visible transform, removes the old attachment, creates a one-user replacement, restores the snapshot, and uses zero size plus one remaining life unit as its failure fallback.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ParticleRen.value: A null particle or a particle without an AppSRT is left unchanged. Otherwise the particle transitions from its old AppSRT attachment to a fresh attachment carrying identical transform values. If allocation fails after the old attachment has been removed, the particle enters a terminal visual state with no wait, zero size, and one remaining life unit.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ParticleRen.rationale: The outer guard makes both null cases no-ops. The successful branch performs the detach-and-replace transition, whereas the failure branch executes only after detachment and writes values that suppress the particle and leave it with minimal remaining lifetime.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_PtclAppSRTH.value: The particle system supplies an HSD_Generator. The callback reads gen->cmdList and compares it by pointer identity with the cmdList fields of ptclref_804D0E5C bank-0 entries 0x96, 0x97, 0x98, and 0x21B. For each match it passes the generator and lbl_803BF810 to hsd_8039D1E4, which stores the vector in gen->userfunc.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_PtclAppSRTH.rationale: The head definition corrects the input type from HSD_Particle to HSD_Generator and removes the former layout cast. Its command-list checks and the callee's userfunc assignment otherwise preserve the standing flow.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_PtclAppSRTH.value: Provides definition-specific participation in the particle system's application-level scale, rotation, and translation handling: only generators for particle effects 0x96, 0x97, 0x98, and 0x21B receive the shared user-function vector.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_PtclAppSRTH.rationale: Initialization still registers the routine in the generator hook slot, and the corrected HSD_Generator definition restricts installation of the AppSRT-related callback vector to four concrete effect definitions.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_PtclAppSRTH.value: Generator hook callback with signature void (HSD_Generator* gen). efLib_Init registers it in the particle system's global generator-hook slot.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_PtclAppSRTH.rationale: The head header and implementation both accept HSD_Generator*, while the baselib global hook slot has the same function-pointer type. This preserves the corrected generator-hook interpretation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_PtclAppSRTH.value: Selectively installs the common AppSRT-related particle user-function vector on generators belonging to effect definitions 0x96, 0x97, 0x98, or 0x21B; generators using any other command list are left unchanged.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_PtclAppSRTH.rationale: The corrected head implementation accepts a generator, compares its command list with four bank-0 definitions, and invokes the userfunc setter only on a match.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_PtclAppSRTH.value: A generator whose command list matches one of the four selected definitions transitions to having userfunc set to lbl_803BF810. A generator with any other command list undergoes no mutation. The checks are independent and contain no timer, allocation, or failure state.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_PtclAppSRTH.rationale: The target contains four independent guarded setter calls and no fallback branch; the callee performs only the userfunc assignment.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SPtcl.value: Receives a particle link number, resource bank, graphics ID, and source JObj from the JObj SPtcl callback path. It discards linkNo, tests bank, and forwards bank, gfx_id, and jobj unchanged to either grLib_801C99C0 or efLib_SpawnParticleEffect, supplying 0 as the final mode flag in both paths.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SPtcl.rationale: The head initialization and callback body preserve the upstream registration, unused link number, bank-controlled routing, unchanged forwarded values, and constant-zero mode.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SPtcl.value: SPtcl callback with signature void (s32 linkNo, s32 bank, s32 gfx_id, HSD_JObj* jobj); linkNo is accepted to satisfy the callback interface but is unused by this implementation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SPtcl.rationale: The head header and definition preserve the complete four-argument SPtcl signature. The body does not read linkNo and uses only bank, gfx_id, and jobj.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SPtcl.value: Serves as the effect library's registered SPtcl callback, routing static-particle requests from JObj display processing either to the ground library for the reserved stage-effect bank 0x1E or to the general particle-effect spawner for every other bank.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SPtcl.rationale: The function remains registered as the SPtcl callback and still routes bank 0x1E to the ground-library handler while sending all other banks to the general spawner with static mode.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetJObjOffs.value: Receives the EF_Effect from efLib_Update, follows effect->gobj to the effect root JObj and then its child pointer, reads the child's current translation.z, adds 2.0, and writes the accumulated value back through the JObj translation setter.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetJObjOffs.rationale: The current updater still passes the EF_Effect to its stored callback, and this callback preserves the root-to-child traversal and Z read-modify-write.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetJObjOffs.value: Effect update callback with signature void (EF_Effect* effect).
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetJObjOffs.rationale: The head definition remains void(EF_Effect*), and the central effect updater invokes its optional callback with exactly that pointer.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetJObjOffs.value: Acts as an effect-update callback that moves the effect model's first child JObj forward by 2.0 units along its local Z axis on every invocation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetJObjOffs.rationale: The current function still selects the effect root's first child and increments its Z translation, and the central updater establishes recurring effect-update invocation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetJObjOffs.value: Its transform change is cumulative rather than a fixed assignment: every active update adds another 2.0 to the first child JObj's Z translation. The callback is skipped while the containing effect is paused because efLib_Update returns before callback dispatch in the paused state.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetJObjOffs.rationale: The callback still reads the current Z value before adding 2.0, while efLib_Update still returns from the paused state before animation or custom callback dispatch.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffsetY_.value: Reads `effect->gobj` to obtain the destination effect JObj, passes `effect->attach_jobj` to `lb_8000B1CC` to produce a base position vector, adds `effect->params.y` to the vector's Y component, and sends the completed vector to `HSD_JObjSetTranslate` as the destination JObj's new translation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffsetY_.rationale: These inputs, transformation, and output are explicit and sequential in the matched body: destination lookup, attachment-derived vector production, scalar Y addition, and JObj translation assignment.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffsetY_.value: Function with signature `void efLib_Cb_SetOffsetY_FromParamY(EF_Effect* effect)`; it consumes one mutable effect instance, updates the translation of that effect's JObj in place, and returns no value.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffsetY_.rationale: The matched definition supplies the exact return and parameter types. Its body dereferences the EF_Effect to obtain the attachment, parameter vector, and effect GObj, then mutates the associated JObj through `HSD_JObjSetTranslate` without returning a result.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffsetY_.value: Positions an effect relative to its attachment by placing the effect's root JObj at an attachment-derived position with the effect parameter's Y component added as a vertical offset.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffsetY_.rationale: The matched body obtains a position from `effect->attach_jobj`, adds `effect->params.y` only to that position's Y coordinate, and assigns the resulting translation to the JObj owned by the effect GObj. This directly establishes an attachment-relative vertical positioning role.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffset_F.value: On each active effect update, the callback reads the JObj's current X/Y/Z translation and the effect's parameter vector, subtracts 0.1 from params.y in place, then writes X + params.x, Y + the updated params.y, and Z + params.z back to the JObj. The mutated Y parameter is retained in EF_Effect and therefore becomes the vertical increment consumed by the next invocation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffset_F.rationale: The head callback preserves the complete translation and persistent-parameter mutation sequence, while efLib_Update continues to dispatch the stored callback on active updates.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffset_F.value: Effect update callback with signature void (EF_Effect*); it requires effect->gobj to hold an HSD_JObj and treats effect->params as a three-component per-update translation delta.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffset_F.rationale: The function's declared argument and return type directly establish the callback signature. It obtains an HSD_JObj from effect->gobj and uses the three floating-point parameter components as additive translation values.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffset_F.value: Acts as an effect-update callback that moves an effect's JObj by its stored per-axis offsets each update while applying a fixed downward acceleration to the Y offset.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffset_F.rationale: The callback still adds all three parameter components to the current JObj translation after reducing params.y by 0.1, and efLib_Update establishes that this operation recurs for active effects.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffset_F.value: Repeated invocations integrate a discrete gravity-like trajectory: X and Z advance by their stored offsets, while the Y increment decreases by 0.1 before every position update. Thus vertical motion progressively bends downward, with params.y crossing through zero and becoming increasingly negative unless another routine changes it.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetOffset_F.rationale: Because each call permanently decreases params.y and then adds that new value to the current Y position, the callback implements constant negative vertical acceleration in discrete updates. The X and Z parameters are read but not changed by this routine, so their contributions remain constant absent external mutation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYAndT.value: The callback reads `effect->user_data`, `effect->gobj`, `expire_flags`, and `lifetime`. A non-null user-data JObj contributes the sign of `scale.x`, which becomes a root-model Y rotation of -π/2 for negative scale and +π/2 otherwise. The expiration branch writes lifetime 11, clears `effect->update`, and requests animation frame 65 across the effect's JObj hierarchy; otherwise, lifetime 1 is rewritten to 6 and frame 60 is requested across that hierarchy.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYAndT.rationale: The callback directly contains each read, transformation, and write. The resolved HSD_JObjReqAnimAll implementation confirms that frames 65 and 60 are propagated from the effect root to animation controllers throughout its non-instanced JObj hierarchy.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYAndT.value: Effect-update callback with signature `void efLib_Cb_SetRotYAndTransition(EF_Effect* effect)`. It mutates the supplied EF_Effect and the root HSD_JObj owned by `effect->gobj`; for this callback, `effect->user_data` is interpreted as a nullable `HSD_JObj*` whose `scale.x` supplies a facing or mirroring sign.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYAndT.rationale: The matched definition establishes the exact callback signature. Its accesses show that the argument is mutable EF_Effect state, that GET_JOBJ retrieves the affected model root, and that user_data is cast to HSD_JObj and read through its X-scale field when non-null.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYAndT.value: Orients an effect model according to the horizontal mirroring of a user-data JObj, then controls a short animation transition: effects eligible for the immediate transition switch to animation frame 65 and become scheduled for removal, while the alternate lifetime-triggered path switches to frame 60 and extends the remaining lifetime.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYAndT.rationale: The current callback still maps user-data scale sign to a signed quarter-turn Y rotation and preserves both lifetime and animation transition branches. The central updater confirms that finite lifetime is the removal countdown.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYAndT.value: The callback has two transition modes. When `expire_flags` is not `EF_DOES_NOT_EXPIRE`, its first invocation makes the transition one-shot by setting lifetime to 11, clearing the update callback, and requesting animation frame 65; subsequent effect updates count that lifetime down to removal without invoking this callback again. When the flag equals `EF_DOES_NOT_EXPIRE`, the callback remains installed, and an invocation that observes lifetime 1 changes it to 6 and requests animation frame 60. A null user-data pointer suppresses only the orientation update, not either transition mode.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYAndT.rationale: The callback's current guards and writes preserve both modes and the limited scope of the user-data null check. efLib_Update preserves pre-dispatch lifetime decrement, zero-lifetime removal, and optional callback invocation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.value: Reads `effect->parent_gobj` to obtain the owning Fighter and `effect->gobj` to obtain the rendered HSD_JObj. It computes `M_PI_2_F - fighter->mv.co.common.x4.x`, tests `fighter->facing_dir`, and writes the effect JObj's Y and Z rotations: negative-facing fighters receive Y = -π/2 and Z = +(π/2 - x4.x), while nonnegative-facing fighters receive Y = +π/2 and Z = -(π/2 - x4.x).
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.rationale: Every input lookup, arithmetic operation, facing-direction branch, and output rotation assignment is explicit in the matched body. The paired signs show that both the base orientation and angular tilt are mirrored across facing directions.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.value: Effect-update callback with signature `void (EF_Effect* effect)`; it mutates the JObj owned by the supplied effect and returns no value.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.rationale: The definition has a void return and one `EF_Effect*` parameter, and its body mutates the effect's JObj. The current generic updater invokes stored callbacks with the corresponding effect pointer.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.value: Acts as an EF_Effect update callback that reorients an effect model to its owning fighter, mirroring the model for the fighter's facing direction and tilting it according to an action-specific angle stored in the fighter's common motion variables.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.rationale: The current updater dispatches effect-specific callbacks, while this callback reads its parent fighter's facing direction and motion variable and writes mirrored Y and Z rotations to the effect JObj.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.value: Each invocation overwrites the effect JObj's Y and Z orientation rather than incrementing it. The fighter's facing sign selects one of two mirrored states: left-facing uses negative quarter-turn Y and positive computed Z tilt, while right-facing or zero uses positive quarter-turn Y and negative computed Z tilt.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.rationale: Both branches call rotation setters with absolute values derived from π/2 and the current fighter variable; neither branch reads the JObj's prior rotations. The branch condition therefore produces two mirrored orientation states on every callback execution.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.value: The callback resolves the rendered JObj from effect->gobj, reads facing_dir from the Fighter stored on effect->parent_gobj, and reads effect->params.z. For negative facing it writes rotation Y = -π/2 and rotation Z = params.z; otherwise it writes rotation Y = +π/2 and rotation Z = -params.z.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.rationale: Each input and output is directly visible in the two branches. The branch reverses both the quarter-turn around Y and the sign applied to the stored Z parameter, yielding mirrored rotation pairs for the two fighter orientations.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.value: Realizes facing-dependent mirroring of a fighter-owned visual effect: changing the fighter between left- and right-facing orientations flips the effect's Y orientation and reverses its parameterized Z tilt so the presentation remains aligned with the fighter.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.rationale: The code selects opposite Y quarter-turns and opposite signs of the same Z-angle parameter solely from the parent fighter's facing_dir. That paired inversion is the transform-level implementation of mirroring a visual effect across fighter facing.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.value: Effect update/configuration callback with signature void (EF_Effect* effect); it mutates the HSD_JObj associated with effect->gobj and expects effect->parent_gobj to contain Fighter user data.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.rationale: The function's declared return and parameter types establish the callback signature. Its GET_JOBJ and GET_FIGHTER accesses establish the required object relationships and show that its output consists solely of mutations to the effect's JObj rotation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.value: Orients an effect's JObj to the parent fighter's facing direction while applying the effect's Z-rotation parameter with the corresponding mirrored sign.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotYZ_Fr.rationale: The callback obtains the JObj owned by the effect, reads the parent fighter's facing direction, and writes paired Y and Z rotations. The opposite rotation pairs in the two branches show that its purpose is to orient and mirror the effect rather than update fighter state or effect lifetime.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotY_Fro.value: Reads effect->gobj to obtain the effect JObj and effect->parent_gobj to obtain the owning Fighter. The sign of Fighter.facing_dir is converted to a fixed yaw of −π/2 for negative facing or +π/2 otherwise, then written to the effect JObj through HSD_JObjSetRotationY.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotY_Fro.rationale: Each stage is explicit in the matched body: the two EF_Effect object references lead to the output JObj and input Fighter, the facing-direction comparison selects one of two half-turn-axis angles, and the selected value becomes the JObj's Y rotation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotY_Fro.value: Implements facing-dependent visual-effect orientation: an effect owned by a left-facing fighter is yawed to −90 degrees, while one owned by a right-facing or nonnegative-facing fighter is yawed to +90 degrees.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotY_Fro.rationale: The code maps the gameplay-facing value stored on the parent Fighter directly to opposite fixed Y-axis orientations on the effect model. This grounds the routine in left/right fighter presentation without identifying it with any one move or effect asset.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotY_Fro.value: Effect update callback with signature `void (EF_Effect* effect)`; it mutates the effect's JObj transform in place and returns no value.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotY_Fro.rationale: The matched definition accepts one EF_Effect pointer and returns void. Its body obtains the JObj through effect->gobj and passes that JObj to the Y-rotation setter, while efLib_Update dispatches callbacks using effect->update(effect).

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotY_Fro.value: Orients an effect's JObj around the Y axis according to the owning fighter's current facing direction, so the effect presents the appropriate left- or right-facing orientation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetRotY_Fro.rationale: The callback retrieves the effect's JObj, tests the parent fighter's facing-direction sign, and writes either negative or positive π/2 as the JObj's Y rotation. The effect library's update routine invokes an effect-specific update callback after animation, establishing this as an effect-orientation callback rather than a general fighter-state operation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScaleRot.value: Reads the parent GObj and effect GObj from EF_Effect, obtains each GObj's JObj, and reads the Fighter from the parent GObj. It component-wise multiplies the parent JObj scale by the effect JObj's existing scale and writes the result back to the effect JObj; it then maps parent Fighter facing_dir < 0 to −π/2 and all other values to +π/2 and writes that angle as the effect JObj's Y rotation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScaleRot.rationale: Each input, transformation, branch, and output is explicit in the matched function body: the two JObj scales feed three component multiplications, while the fighter's facing direction controls the signed half-pi rotation supplied to the effect JObj.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScaleRot.value: Effect callback with signature void (EF_Effect* effect); the argument must identify an effect whose gobj and parent_gobj both carry JObjs, with parent_gobj carrying Fighter user data.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScaleRot.rationale: The function's declared parameter and return type establish the callback signature. Its unconditional GET_JOBJ accesses on effect->gobj and effect->parent_gobj, followed by GET_FIGHTER on the parent, establish the object-shape requirements.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScaleRot.value: Configures a fighter-owned effect model so that its scale incorporates the owning fighter model's scale and its Y-axis orientation follows the fighter's facing direction.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScaleRot.rationale: The callback obtains the parent fighter and effect JObjs, multiplies their scale components and writes the product to the effect JObj, then selects negative or positive π/2 from the fighter's facing direction and applies that as the effect's Y rotation. These operations make the effect visually inherit the fighter's presentation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScale_Fr.value: Reads the scale factor from `effect->params.x` and obtains the destination JObj from `effect->gobj`. For each axis, it reads the JObj's current scale, multiplies that component by the parameter, and passes the result to the corresponding X, Y, or Z scale setter.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScale_Fr.rationale: The matched statements expose the complete input-to-output path: `params.x` supplies the common factor, `GET_JOBJ(effect->gobj)` supplies the transformed object, and paired per-axis getters and setters perform the read-modify-write operations.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScale_Fr.value: Effect callback with signature `void efLib_Cb_SetScale_FromParamX(EF_Effect* effect)`; it mutates the JObj associated with the supplied effect and returns no value.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScale_Fr.rationale: The matched definition has one mutable `EF_Effect*` parameter and a `void` return type, and its body reaches the effect's GObj-backed JObj and changes that object's scale in place.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScale_Fr.value: Uniformly scales an effect's associated JObj in all three dimensions using the effect's X parameter as a multiplicative scale factor.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScale_Fr.rationale: The matched callback obtains the JObj attached to the effect GObj, multiplies each of its current X, Y, and Z scale components by the same `effect->params.x` value, and writes all three results back.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScale_Fr.value: Applies an immediate, unguarded multiplicative update to the JObj's current scale. Because it uses the current components rather than fixed base values, repeated invocations compound the scaling; a factor of 1 leaves the scale unchanged and a factor of 0 collapses all three components to zero.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_SetScale_Fr.rationale: Each axis is read before being multiplied and written back, with no reset, clamp, or conditional guard in the callback. Those operations establish cumulative multiplicative behavior and the stated identity and zero-factor cases.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftCo_Bury.value: Reads effect->gobj and effect->parent_gobj from its EF_Effect argument and forwards them, in that order, to ftCo_800C0FCC; it produces no direct return value or local state change.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftCo_Bury.rationale: The complete body consists solely of the call ftCo_800C0FCC(effect->gobj, effect->parent_gobj), establishing both field reads, their argument order, and the absence of other local processing.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftCo_Bury.value: Realizes the effect-side integration for Melee's buried status, a restraining fighter condition whose duration can be reduced through button mashing.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftCo_Bury.rationale: The callback and its sole callee are explicitly associated with ftCo_Bury, grounding the code in fighter burial behavior. SmashWiki independently characterizes being buried as a control-restraining condition affected by button mashing; the callback should therefore be understood as the visual-effect bridge into that mechanic, not as the routine that implements the status timer itself.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftCo_Bury.value: Effect update callback with signature void (EF_Effect* effect).
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftCo_Bury.rationale: The definition directly establishes the signature, and the generic effect updater confirms that this function shape is used for stored effect-update callbacks.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftCo_Bury.value: Acts as the effect-library callback adapter for fighter burial behavior: when dispatched by the generic effect updater, it delegates bury-specific coordination to the fighter-common Bury subsystem using the effect object and its owning fighter object.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftCo_Bury.rationale: The generic updater establishes the callback context, and this callback's entire body forwards the effect GObj and parent GObj to the fighter-common Bury helper.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftKp_Specia.value: Reads the primary effect GObj, the next linked EF_Effect's GObj, and the parent fighter. From the fighter it consumes motion_id, command-variable bit 0 of cmd_vars[2], move variable x10, and the current floor normal. It writes JOBJ_HIDDEN on the second effect hierarchy and writes the same Z rotation to both effect hierarchies, using -atan2f(floor.normal.x, floor.normal.y) when both alignment guards pass and 0 otherwise.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftKp_Specia.rationale: Every source and destination is explicit in the matched body: effect->gobj and effect->next->gobj supply the two JObjs, effect->parent_gobj supplies the Fighter, the fighter fields determine visibility and rotation, and the only outputs are JObj flags and rotations.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftKp_Specia.value: Implements terrain-relative visual presentation for Bowser's Whirling Fortress, including a grounded-only effect component and slope alignment of the move's paired effect models.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftKp_Specia.rationale: The function is explicitly the Koopa SpecialHi effect callback and distinguishes the grounded SpecialHi motion while orienting its effects from the floor normal. SmashWiki identifies Bowser's up special as Whirling Fortress and documents grounded and aerial forms in Melee.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftKp_Specia.value: An effect-specific per-frame update callback with signature void (EF_Effect* effect).
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftKp_Specia.rationale: The function directly takes an `EF_Effect*` and returns void, while the current generic updater dispatches callbacks of this form during ordinary active-effect processing.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftKp_Specia.value: Updates the paired effect models attached to Bowser's SpecialHi: it shows the second model only during motion 359 and, when the move's script and collision state request terrain alignment, rotates both models to match the current floor slope.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftKp_Specia.rationale: The current callback obtains two effect JObjs, toggles the second hierarchy from motion ID 359, and either applies a floor-normal-derived rotation to both hierarchies or resets both to zero. The move references identify Bowser's up special as Whirling Fortress without relying on the removed fighter-source span.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftKp_Specia.value: During motion 359, the callback clears JOBJ_HIDDEN on the second effect hierarchy; in every other motion it hides that hierarchy. Independently, it aligns both effect hierarchies to the floor only while cmd_vars[2] bit 0 is set and move variable x10 is nonzero; if either guard fails, it restores both Z rotations to zero.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftKp_Specia.rationale: The complete current callback contains these two independent branches and explicitly writes every visibility and rotation state. Removing the unsupported grounded-state label avoids depending on the deleted fighter-source citation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftLg_Specia.value: The callback resolves the effect root from effect->gobj and its second child as root->child->next, then resolves the owning Fighter from effect->parent_gobj. fighter->motion_id drives that child's JOBJ_HIDDEN flag; fighter->cmd_vars[3] and fighter->mv.co.common.x4.z gate slope alignment; and the fighter's floor-normal X/Y components are converted with -atan2f into the root JObj's Z rotation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftLg_Specia.rationale: Every stated input-to-output path is explicit in the matched body: the effect and parent GObjs provide the two object graphs, the motion and move fields select visual behavior, and the collision normal is transformed into the written rotation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftLg_Specia.value: Realizes the visual adaptation of Luigi Cyclone, Luigi's down special, keeping its spawned cyclone graphic appropriate to the current move motion and aligned with sloped ground when the move enables collision-following presentation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftLg_Specia.rationale: The current callback is specific to Luigi's SpecialLw and updates effect visibility and slope-relative rotation from fighter state. SmashWiki identifies Luigi Cyclone as Luigi's down special and documents its grounded and aerial presentations.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftLg_Specia.value: Effect-update callback with signature void (EF_Effect*): the argument supplies both the effect GObj whose JObj hierarchy is mutated and the parent fighter GObj whose move and collision state drive the update.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftLg_Specia.rationale: The matched definition has a void return and one EF_Effect pointer parameter. Its body obtains the rendered JObj from effect->gobj and the Fighter from effect->parent_gobj, establishing the semantic callback shape.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftLg_Specia.value: Updates the model presentation of Luigi's Cyclone effect: it selects a motion-specific child visual and, when the move's script and collision state request it, rotates the effect root to follow the floor slope.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftLg_Specia.rationale: The current body toggles a child hierarchy based on motion ID and conditionally sets the root's Z rotation from the floor normal. SmashWiki supplies the durable identification of Luigi's down special as Luigi Cyclone after the old fighter-source span disappeared.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftLg_Specia.value: On each callback, motion 357 makes the effect's second child subtree visible and every other motion hides it. Independently, simultaneous nonzero values in cmd_vars[3] and mv.co.common.x4.z enable floor-slope rotation; if either guard is zero, the effect is restored to zero Z rotation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftLg_Specia.rationale: The first conditional clears or sets JOBJ_HIDDEN solely from motion_id, and the second conditional either writes the negative floor-normal angle or explicitly writes 0.0. These branches completely describe the callback's state-dependent behavior.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftMr_Specia.value: Reads the effect GObj's root JObj and selects the root's second child subtree, then reads motion_id, cmd_vars[3], a common move-state word, and the collision floor normal from the Fighter stored on effect->parent_gobj. It writes JOBJ_HIDDEN across the selected subtree and writes the root JObj's Z rotation, using `-atan2f(floor.normal.x, floor.normal.y)` when both move-state guards are nonzero and zero otherwise.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftMr_Specia.rationale: Every input and output is explicit in the matched body: effect ownership supplies the Fighter, hierarchy links select the visibility subtree, fighter state controls both branches, and the only mutations are subtree flags and root rotation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftMr_Specia.value: Realizes the dynamic visual behavior of Mario Tornado, Mario's down-special move in Melee, by selecting move-state-specific effect geometry and allowing the effect to visually conform to sloped ground.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftMr_Specia.rationale: The code is explicitly specialized to `ftMr_SpecialLw`, reads Mario's down-special fighter state, and updates only its effect hierarchy. SmashWiki independently identifies Mario Tornado as Mario's down special in Melee, grounding the internal character/move designation in the named game mechanic.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftMr_Specia.value: Effect-update callback with signature `void efLib_Cb_ftMr_SpecialLw(EF_Effect* effect)`; the argument identifies a mutable effect whose GObj owns the rendered JObj hierarchy and whose parent_gobj identifies the owning Fighter.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftMr_Specia.rationale: The matched definition supplies the return and parameter types. Its accesses through effect->gobj and effect->parent_gobj establish the two object relationships and show that the callback mutates the effect's JObj hierarchy without returning a value.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftMr_Specia.value: Updates the model presentation of Mario's down-special effect: it conditionally reveals one effect subtree for motion state 349 and rotates the effect root to follow the owning fighter's floor normal when the move's control flags request slope alignment.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftMr_Specia.rationale: The complete matched body obtains the effect's root JObj and a specific descendant subtree, reads the owning Fighter, toggles JOBJ_HIDDEN according to motion_id 349, and conditionally derives the root's Z rotation from the floor normal. These operations make the routine a presentation callback specialized to the move rather than a general effect update.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftMr_Specia.value: When the owning Fighter's motion_id is 349, the callback clears JOBJ_HIDDEN recursively on the selected effect subtree; in every other motion it sets JOBJ_HIDDEN recursively. Independently, it aligns the effect root to the floor only while both cmd_vars[3] and the tested common move-state word are nonzero; if either guard is zero, it restores the root's Z rotation to 0 radians.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Cb_ftMr_Specia.rationale: The function contains two independent guarded state updates. The first is an exact motion-ID visibility switch, while the second chooses between a floor-normal-derived angle and a neutral rotation based on the conjunction of two fighter-state values.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Create.value: The graphics ID selects `efAsync_DatEntries[gfx_id / 1000].data[gfx_id % 1000]` as an EF_EffectDesc. Descriptor model and animation pointers are loaded into a new JObj hierarchy, while descriptor lifetime is converted to an integer effect lifetime. The parent argument and current load kind are stored in the EF_Effect, which becomes GObj user data with `efLib_remove_user_data` as its cleanup callback; the JObj becomes the GObj object, and the GObj is registered for JObj rendering and `efLib_Update` processing.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Create.rationale: The current complete body preserves each stage from descriptor lookup through effect allocation, ownership storage, GObj and JObj setup, animation loading, rendering linkage, and update registration.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Create.value: Signature: `EF_Effect* efLib_Create(int gfx_id, HSD_GObj* parent_gobj)`. `gfx_id` is a decimal-packed effect descriptor identifier whose quotient and remainder by 1000 select an asynchronous data-table entry and descriptor index; `parent_gobj` records the effect's owning GObj and is required for asynchronous effects. The return is the newly allocated effect or NULL when effect allocation, GObj creation, or JObj loading fails.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Create.rationale: The current definition supplies the signature, graphics-ID decomposition, parent assignment and asynchronous-parent assertion, along with explicit failure returns and the successful effect return.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Create.value: Creates a descriptor-backed effect instance for a graphics ID, giving it an effect GObj, render linkage, JObj model and animations, cleanup metadata, and a per-frame update process so callers can subsequently attach or configure it.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Create.rationale: The current implementation resolves an effect descriptor, allocates and initializes effect state, creates and configures the effect GObj, loads the model and optional animations, and installs the common updater.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Create.value: A new effect starts active, non-expiring by flag, without inherited scale, unattached, and without a custom update callback. In asynchronous load mode, creation enforces a 64-effect policy by removing the last effect when the count is already at least 64, then increments the count. Graphics IDs 25 and 26 use GObj priority link 12 while all others use link 11. A nonzero descriptor lifetime is stored with one extra update tick; optional animations begin at frame 0 and their JObjs are queued for animation processing.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_Create.rationale: The current constructor explicitly initializes these flags and pointers, handles the asynchronous capacity policy, selects the GObj link from the graphics ID, adjusts finite lifetime, and starts optional animations at frame zero.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Maps `gfx_id` to a generator link number—2 for ID 0x121, 1 for IDs 0xFF, 0x7918, 0xFC, and 0xF7, and 0 otherwise—computes the particle bank as `gfx_id / 1000`, and passes the link number, bank, and full ID to `hsd_8039F05C`. On success it copies all three components of `*pos` into `generator->pos`; on failure it propagates null unchanged.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: Every stage of this flow is explicit in the matched body: the switch selects the link number, integer division derives the bank, the three values feed the baselib constructor, and the guarded component assignments initialize the returned generator's position.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: A positional particle-generator factory with signature `HSD_Generator* (s32 gfx_id, Vec3* pos)`. The graphics ID identifies both the particle-data bank and command within that bank; the result is either a newly created generator or null.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The matched declaration fixes the parameter and result types. The body computes `gfx_id / 1000` as the bank while also passing the complete graphics ID to the constructor, then guards all generator field writes with a null check.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Creates a free-standing particle generator for a graphics-effect ID, places it at the requested position, and returns the generator so effect dispatchers can use it as the spawned effect object.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The head implementation derives the particle bank, constructs a generator, conditionally copies the requested position, and returns the nullable result. The current synchronous dispatcher continues routing direct particle-generator graphics-ID ranges to this function.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: The input graphics ID is passed intact to the generator creator while gfx_id / 1000 selects its bank and zero selects the generator link. The resulting generator's appsrt field is read; if empty, status 1 and the generator's idnum flow through psAddGeneratorAppSRT_begin into a newly allocated identity-SRT record stored back in generator->appsrt. Failure flows through generator destruction to a NULL return; otherwise the generator pointer is returned.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The current target shows generator construction, AppSRT lookup, status-1 allocation, cleanup, and return. The current AppSRT implementation shows use of the generator ID, assignment to `generator->appsrt`, and identity-transform initialization.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Spawns a visual-effect particle generator with application-controlled scale, rotation, and translation state: it preserves an existing transform record or installs a new identity transform for later effect-specific positioning, orientation, or scaling.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: Successful construction guarantees an AppSRT record, and the current AppSRT allocator shows that this record carries initialized scale, rotation, and translation components.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Signature: HSD_Generator* efLib_CreateGenerator_AddAppSRT(s32 gfx_id). The return is a nullable generator pointer; every non-NULL result has a non-NULL HSD_psAppSRT in generator->appsrt.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The matched definition establishes the parameter and return types. Its control flow returns NULL when generator creation fails or when AppSRT acquisition fails, and reaches a non-NULL return only after an existing or newly created appsrt pointer has passed the NULL check.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Creates a particle-effect generator for a graphics ID and guarantees that a successfully returned generator has an application-level scale/rotation/translation record, destroying the new generator if that record cannot be obtained.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The function creates a generator, reuses its existing appsrt record or calls psAddGeneratorAppSRT_begin to install one, and invokes the generator-destruction routine before returning NULL when AppSRT acquisition fails.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: There are three completion states: generator creation failure returns NULL immediately; a generator that already owns an AppSRT is returned unchanged; and a generator lacking AppSRT is returned after successful status-1 AppSRT allocation. If that allocation fails, the partially created generator is destroyed and NULL is returned.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The target's nested guards distinguish constructor failure, existing AppSRT, successful allocation, and allocation failure with teardown. The allocator confirms that its result is nullable and installed on the generator.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Passes `gfx_id` and the first variadic `HSD_JObj*` into the shared generator/AppSRT creation helper. On success, it dereferences the next variadic `f32*`, converts only its sign into a discrete facing orientation, stores that orientation in `generator->appsrt->rot.y`, and returns the configured generator.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The helper call consumes the graphics identifier and JObj attachment input and writes the resulting generator through a local pointer. The guarded branch then maps a negative direction to -π/2 and every nonnegative direction to +π/2 before exposing the generator to the caller.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: A variadic generator-construction callback with signature `HSD_Generator* (s32 gfx_id, va_list vlist)`. Its argument payload begins with an `HSD_JObj*`, followed by an `f32*` facing-direction value that is consumed only if generator creation succeeds; it returns the created generator or `NULL`.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The declaration fixes the callback signature and return type. The two `va_arg` expressions establish the ordered payload types, while the null guard shows that the second argument is conditionally consumed and that creation failure propagates as a null result.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Creates the requested particle generator with an AppSRT associated with a supplied JObj, then orients the generator's application transform to face left or right by setting its Y rotation to -π/2 or +π/2 according to the sign of a facing-direction value.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The function passes the graphics ID and first variadic argument to the generator-and-AppSRT creation helper. After successful creation, it reads the facing direction and writes one of two quarter-turn Y rotations into the generator's AppSRT, establishing that this is an orientation-configuring generator factory.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: The graphics identifier and first variadic argument, an HSD_JObj pointer, flow into the generator/AppSRT creation helper. If creation succeeds, the next argument's pointed-to float is reduced to its sign and written as appsrt->rot.y (-π/2 for negative, +π/2 otherwise); the final pointed-to float is replicated into appsrt->scale.x, scale.y, and scale.z. The configured generator pointer is returned.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The matched body directly exposes the argument-consumption order, helper inputs, sign-to-rotation conversion, uniform scale replication, and returned output.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Implements particle-system scale/rotation/translation presentation for a directional visual effect: the effect is turned to one of two opposite Y-axis orientations according to facing sign and is resized uniformly without changing the AppSRT translation established at creation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The target writes only AppSRT Y rotation and scale, selecting opposite quarter-turns from the direction sign and broadcasting one scale to every axis. The AppSRT implementation establishes these fields as parts of the generator's application transform.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Signature: HSD_Generator* efLib_CreateGenerator_AppSRT_SetFacingDirScale(s32 gfx_id, va_list vlist). The variadic payload is consumed in order as HSD_JObj*, f32* direction, and f32* uniform scale. The returned HSD_Generator* may be NULL when generator/AppSRT creation fails.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The declaration gives the fixed signature, while the three va_arg operations establish the exact payload order and pointer types. The explicit generator-null branch and nullable generator creation routines in the same unit establish the nullable return contract.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Creates a JObj-associated particle generator with application-level transform state, then configures that state so the generated effect faces according to a signed direction and uses a caller-supplied uniform scale.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The function passes the graphics identifier and variadic JObj to the generator/AppSRT creation helper. On success, it converts the direction sign into a Y rotation of negative or positive π/2 and copies one scale value into all three scale axes.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Transform configuration is conditional on successful generator creation: a NULL generator is returned without consuming the direction or scale arguments. On success, any direction strictly below zero selects -π/2 Y rotation, while zero and positive values select +π/2, and all three scale components are overwritten with the same supplied value.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The generator-null guard encloses both later va_arg operations and all AppSRT writes. The ternary uses a strict less-than-zero comparison, and the chained assignment overwrites each scale axis.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: The function creates a generic effect with descriptor ID 0 under gobj, stores jobj in effect->attach_jobj and a value copy of *vec in effect->params, and attaches the gfx_id-selected generator to GET_JOBJ(effect->gobj). During later active effect updates, efLib_Cb_AccumOffset_FromParams reads the attachment's current translation, adds the stored x/y/z offset, and writes the sum to the effect JObj; the attached generator consequently receives that moving transform through its AppSRT-enabled attachment.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: At head, the creator still stores the attachment and copied offset and invokes the attached-generator helper. The helper creates the generator on the effect JObj and establishes AppSRT state, while the installed callback and generic updater preserve the later attachment-plus-offset flow.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Realizes a following visual particle effect with a configurable positional offset: the effect tracks a model joint or other JObj anchor while its generator uses application-level scale/rotation/translation state.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The current callback maps an anchor's current translation plus a stored offset onto the JObj carrying the attached particle generator, and the AppSRT implementation establishes the generator's application transform state.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Signature: EF_Effect* efLib_CreateGenerator_AppSRT_SetPos(int gfx_id, HSD_GObj* gobj, HSD_JObj* jobj, Vec3* vec). gfx_id selects the attached particle generator, gobj is passed as the effect's parent/owner, jobj is retained as the positional attachment, and vec points to a three-component offset that is copied into the effect rather than retained. The return is the created EF_Effect or NULL when effect creation fails.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The declaration supplies the exact C types. The body passes gfx_id to generator creation, gobj to efLib_Create, stores jobj in attach_jobj, copies *vec into params, and returns efLib_Create's nullable result.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Creates an owner-managed effect that anchors a particle generator to the effect's JObj and continuously positions that JObj at an attachment JObj's world-space translation plus a caller-supplied offset.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The head creator stores the attachment and copied offset, installs the offset-accumulation callback, and calls the helper that creates an AppSRT-enabled generator attached to the effect JObj. The callback then maps the attachment's current translation plus that offset onto the effect JObj.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: If efLib_Create fails, the function returns NULL without initializing an attachment or generator. Once an effect exists, it is returned even if generator creation or AppSRT allocation fails; the helper destroys an AppSRT-less generator and nulls only its local output. For a successfully configured effect, each active update recomputes its position from the attachment and fixed offset, while the library's paused state suppresses that callback and therefore freezes this positional following until updates resume.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The head creator guards all setup on successful effect allocation but does not inspect the helper's generator result. The helper destroys and nulls a generator when AppSRT allocation fails, and the generic update routine returns in the paused state before dispatching the positional callback.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: gfx_id and the first variadic value, an HSD_JObj pointer, flow into generator creation. If that produces a generator, the float addressed by the next variadic value is read once and propagated equally to generator->appsrt->scale.x, scale.y, and scale.z; the resulting generator pointer is returned to the asynchronous effect dispatcher.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The matched body exposes the complete input-to-output path: the helper receives gfx_id and the extracted JObj, the guarded assignment broadcasts one dereferenced float across the three scale axes, and the function returns the helper's generator result. The call graph identifies efAsync_Dispatch as its caller, consistent with the function's va_list-based dispatch interface.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Realizes uniform sizing of a generated particle visual effect through the scale component of its application-level scale/rotation/translation transform.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The target broadcasts a single supplied value into all three AppSRT scale axes, and the AppSRT implementation confirms these axes are the scale component of the generator-owned application transform.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Signature: HSD_Generator* efLib_CreateGenerator_AppSRT_SetScale(s32 gfx_id, va_list vlist). Its variadic schema begins with HSD_JObj*; if generator creation succeeds, the next argument is f32* and points to the scalar copied into AppSRT scale.x, scale.y, and scale.z. The return value is the created HSD_Generator or NULL on creation failure.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The declaration supplies the exact formal signature. The two va_arg expressions establish the variadic argument types and their order, while the success guard and returned generator establish the nullable return contract and show that the f32 pointer is consumed only after successful creation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Creates a particle generator for the requested graphics effect, associates it with a JObj and an application-SRT record, and, on successful creation, initializes that record with a caller-supplied uniform scale.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The current function passes the graphics ID and variadic JObj to the generator/AppSRT helper and, on success, writes the next variadic scalar to every AppSRT scale axis.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: The JObj argument is consumed before creation is attempted. If creation fails, the function returns NULL without consuming the scale argument or writing transform state. If creation succeeds, it immediately replaces the AppSRT record's identity unit scale with the supplied uniform value and returns the generator.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The first variadic extraction occurs in the helper call, while the scale extraction and writes are guarded by a non-null generator. The AppSRT allocator initializes new records to unit scale.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Passes a zero-valued leading option, gfx_id / 1000, the full gfx_id, and the attachment JObj to hsd_8039EFAC. It preserves that callee's HSD_Generator pointer as its return value; when non-null, the pointer is also used to update the generator's type field before being returned.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The source exposes the complete input-to-output path without intermediate transformations beyond deriving the graphics group and clearing one type bit. The archived assembly independently shows the division-derived argument, call, null guard, halfword mask at offset 0x16, and unchanged pointer return in r3.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: HSD_Generator* (s32 gfx_id, HSD_JObj* jobj). The graphics identifier is also partitioned into a group index by integer division by 1000, and the return value is nullable when generator creation fails.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The matched declaration directly establishes the parameter and return types. The construction call passes gfx_id / 1000 as a separate selector, and the explicit null check establishes that the returned HSD_Generator pointer may be null.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Creates the particle generator identified by a graphics-effect ID, attaches it to a supplied JObj, and configures the successfully created generator by clearing its PSAPPSRT_UNK_B10 type flag.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The matched function delegates generator construction to hsd_8039EFAC with the graphics ID and attachment JObj, conditionally clears a generator type bit, and returns the resulting generator. This establishes that it is an attached-generator creation wrapper with one post-creation configuration step.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Generator creation has two result branches: a null result is returned without further work, while a successful result has PSAPPSRT_UNK_B10 cleared in its type flags before it is returned.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The sole guard tests the constructed generator pointer. Only the non-null branch mutates generator state, making successful versus failed creation the function's complete state-dependent behavior.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: The function sends 0, gfx_id / 1000, gfx_id, and jobj to the generator constructor. On success it reads generator->appsrt, creates and installs an identity AppSRT record with status 0 only when that field is NULL, writes generator into appsrt->gp, clears generator type bits 0x600, and sets PSAPPSRT_UNK_B11. If no AppSRT is available, it destroys the newly created generator and returns NULL.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The current target directly establishes constructor inputs, AppSRT reuse or allocation, the back-link, type writes, and failure cleanup. The AppSRT implementation confirms installation and identity initialization.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Realizes an attached visual particle effect whose generator can be transformed through application-controlled scale, rotation, and translation state relative to a scene JObj.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The target constructs a particle generator with a JObj attachment and equips it with AppSRT state; the AppSRT allocator shows that state contains initialized scale, rotation, and translation components.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Signature: HSD_Generator* efLib_CreateGenerator_Attach_AddAppSRT(s32 gfx_id, HSD_JObj* jobj). gfx_id is forwarded intact as the generator effect identifier and is also divided by 1000 for a separate constructor argument; jobj is the attachment object. The return is the created HSD_Generator or NULL when generator creation or required AppSRT setup fails.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The current definition provides the exact types, demonstrates both graphics-ID uses and the JObj attachment argument, and contains explicit null-result paths for construction and AppSRT failure.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Creates a particle generator attached to a supplied JObj, ensures that the generator has an application-level scale/rotation/translation record, back-links that record to the generator, and enables the generator's AppSRT mode.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The current body passes the JObj to the generator constructor, reuses or creates AppSRT state, assigns `appsrt->gp`, and normalizes the generator's AppSRT type bits.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Generator creation failure leaves no object and returns NULL. After successful generator creation, an existing AppSRT record is retained; otherwise a status-0 record is allocated. AppSRT allocation failure immediately destroys the generator and returns NULL. Every successful return guarantees a non-NULL generator->appsrt whose gp points back to that generator, with type bits 0x600 cleared and PSAPPSRT_UNK_B11 set.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The current nested guards define constructor failure, existing-state reuse, allocation failure with teardown, and successful normalization of the generator/AppSRT relationship and type flags.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: `gfx_id` and the `HSD_JObj*` consumed from `vlist` flow into generator creation with an AppSRT. If that produces a generator, the function reads `GET_JOBJ(gobj)` into a temporary `Vec3` scale and broadcasts `scale.y` to `generator->appsrt->scale.x`, `.y`, and `.z`; it then returns the generator without further mutation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The matched body directly exposes both input paths: the ID and variadic JObj feed the creation helper, while the GObj's JObj feeds the scale read. The chained assignments demonstrate that only the Y component is consumed and that it becomes a uniform generator scale, with the null check preventing writes after failed creation.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: An effect-construction helper with signature `HSD_Generator* (s32 gfx_id, va_list vlist, HSD_GObj* gobj)`. Its variadic contract consumes one `HSD_JObj*` attachment target; `gobj` supplies the scale to inherit, and the result is either the created generator or null.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The declaration establishes the formal signature and result type. The body performs exactly one `va_arg(vlist, HSD_JObj*)`, passes that pointer into generator creation, conditionally dereferences the returned generator, and otherwise returns the null result unchanged.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Creates a particle generator attached to a JObj, equips it with an AppSRT transform, and, when creation succeeds, gives the generator a uniform scale inherited from the Y scale of the supplied GObj's root JObj.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The function passes the graphics ID and first variadic HSD_JObj pointer to the generator-and-AppSRT creation helper. It then guards against creation failure, reads the GObj JObj's scale, and copies its Y component into all three AppSRT scale axes. The synchronous effect dispatcher uses this helper as a complete construction recipe for four graphics-effect IDs.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: gfx_id flows to the generator constructor both directly and as gfx_id / 1000, selecting the effect and its thousand-ID group. The resulting generator supplies an existing appsrt pointer or its idnum to a status-1 AppSRT allocation. On success, translation is copied component-for-component into appsrt->translate; the sign of direction selects appsrt->rot.y and, for the negative case, sets generator kind bit 0x40000. The configured generator is returned to the caller.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The current target shows all generator inputs and output transform writes. The AppSRT implementation confirms allocation from generator ID and status and installation of the resulting record.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Realizes placement and horizontal-facing presentation for a visual particle effect: it positions the effect generator through AppSRT translation and mirrors its orientation according to facing direction by selecting ±90° around Y and marking the negative-facing generator with kind bit 0x40000.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The target writes application-level translation and opposite Y rotations rather than gameplay movement state, and it applies the additional generator kind bit only to the negative-facing branch.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Signature: HSD_Generator* efLib_CreateGenerator_Translate_FacingDir(s32 gfx_id, Vec3* translation, f32 direction). The return is nullable. translation must point to a readable three-component floating-point vector whenever generator creation and AppSRT acquisition succeed. direction is used only as a sign selector: negative values choose the mirrored orientation, while zero and positive values choose the non-mirrored orientation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The matched declaration establishes the exact C types. The body can return NULL after either generator-creation or AppSRT-allocation failure, dereferences translation only on the successful path, and compares direction only against zero rather than consuming its magnitude.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Creates a particle generator for a graphics-effect ID, ensures that it has an application SRT transform, and initializes that transform with a requested translation and a left- or right-facing Y rotation.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The function creates a generator from gfx_id, reuses or allocates its appsrt record, copies all three translation components, and selects a positive or negative quarter-turn around Y from the sign of direction.

main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.value: Creation has three outcomes. If the generator constructor fails, the function returns NULL without reading translation. If the generator exists but has no AppSRT and AppSRT allocation fails, the generator is passed to hsd_8039D4DC and the function returns NULL. Otherwise it retains the existing or newly allocated AppSRT, applies the requested transform, and returns the generator. A negative direction additionally sets kind bit 0x40000 and uses -π/2 Y rotation; a zero or positive direction leaves that bit unchanged and uses +π/2.
main/melee/ef/eflib:efLib_CreateGenerato.rationale: The current nested null checks and cleanup call define the two failure outcomes and successful path, while the final sign branch establishes the two directional transform states.
